text: Colorado should tax higher incomes at higher rates instead of using one flat rate for everyone.
coding_guide: Agree: supports Amendment 87 or a graduated state income tax in Colorado. Disagree: opposes Amendment 87 or wants to keep the flat state income tax. Statements about federal tax brackets do not count.

text: State law should cap Colorado's income tax rate at today's 4.4 percent.
coding_guide: Agree: supports Proposition 136, or pledges to oppose any increase in the state income tax rate. Disagree: opposes Proposition 136, or supports higher state income tax rates for some taxpayers.

text: When Colorado collects more than its TABOR revenue limit, the state should keep the extra for schools instead of refunding it.
coding_guide: Agree: supports Proposition NN or letting the state keep revenue above the TABOR limit for schools and services. Disagree: opposes Proposition NN or wants revenue above the limit refunded to taxpayers.

text: Sales tax collected on sporting goods should be set aside for water, land and wildfire programs.
coding_guide: Agree: supports Proposition 137. Disagree: opposes Proposition 137.

text: The state constitution should protect the right to buy and use natural gas in homes and businesses.
coding_guide: Agree: supports Amendment 82, or opposes limits on natural gas hookups and appliances. Disagree: opposes Amendment 82, or supports limiting new natural gas hookups or appliances.

text: Government should speed up the shift from oil, gas and coal to renewable energy.
coding_guide: Agree: supports a faster move to renewable energy, clean-energy mandates or targets, federal clean-energy tax credits, or limits on new drilling. Disagree: supports expanding oil, gas or coal production, opposes clean-energy mandates, or supported repealing federal clean-energy credits.

text: The state should be able to override local zoning rules to allow more housing to be built.
coding_guide: Agree: supports state laws that preempt local zoning to allow more housing (for example Colorado's 2024 laws on accessory dwelling units, density near transit, or occupancy limits). Disagree: wants zoning decisions left to local governments, or opposed those laws.

text: Government should do more to make sure everyone has health insurance, even if it costs taxpayers more.
coding_guide: Agree: supports expanding coverage, such as extending the enhanced Affordable Care Act premium tax credits, protecting or expanding Medicaid, a public option or Medicare for All. Disagree: supports reducing federal health spending, Medicaid work requirements or cuts, or market-based approaches instead of expanded government coverage.

text: The federal government should keep broad tariffs on imported goods.
coding_guide: Agree: supports the broad tariffs imposed in 2025 and 2026. Disagree: opposes broad tariffs, or voted to end the emergency declarations behind them.

text: Congress was right to pass the 2025 federal tax and spending law known as the One Big Beautiful Bill Act.
coding_guide: Agree: voted for or praised H.R. 1 of the 119th Congress (Public Law 119-21, signed July 4, 2025). Disagree: voted against or criticized it.

text: Federal public lands should stay in federal ownership rather than being sold or transferred.
coding_guide: Agree: opposes selling or transferring federal public lands. Disagree: supports selling federal land or transferring it to states or private owners.

text: Abortion should be legal in all or most cases.
coding_guide: Agree: supports abortion rights, Colorado's Amendment 79 (2024), or the federal Women's Health Protection Act. Disagree: supports bans or new restrictions on abortion. An endorsement or rating from an abortion-rights or anti-abortion group is an interest-group rating.

text: Gun laws should be stricter than they are now.
coding_guide: Agree: supports new gun restrictions, such as Colorado's 2025 permit requirement for certain semiautomatic firearms (SB25-003), an assault weapons ban or wider background checks. Disagree: opposes new restrictions or wants to loosen current ones. An NRA or gun-safety group grade is an interest-group rating.

text: Students should play on school sports teams that match their biological sex, not their gender identity.
coding_guide: Agree: supports Proposition 134 or the federal Protection of Women and Girls in Sports Act. Disagree: opposes Proposition 134 or that act, or supports letting transgender students play on teams matching their gender identity.

text: Colorado should ban surgery that changes the sex characteristics of patients under 18 as treatment for gender identity.
coding_guide: Agree: supports Proposition 135, or supports banning all gender-transition medical care for minors (which includes surgery). Disagree: opposes Proposition 135. Opposing restrictions on gender-affirming care in general, without addressing surgery, is inferred and coded no stronger than 2.

text: Colorado police and jails should notify federal immigration authorities when they charge someone with a serious crime and cannot confirm the person is in the country legally.
coding_guide: Agree: supports Amendment 81, or supports repealing Colorado's limits on local cooperation with federal immigration enforcement in criminal cases. Disagree: opposes Amendment 81 or defends those limits.

text: Deporting people who are in the U.S. without legal status should be a top federal priority.
coding_guide: Agree: supports mass deportation or expanded federal immigration enforcement and funding. Disagree: opposes mass deportation, puts a path to legal status first, or opposes the scale or methods of current enforcement.

text: Fentanyl crimes should carry tougher penalties, including mandatory prison time for selling any amount.
coding_guide: Agree: supports Proposition 132, felony charges for possessing any amount of fentanyl, or mandatory prison for dealing any amount. Disagree: opposes Proposition 132 or prefers current law and treatment-first approaches.

text: Child sex trafficking should be punished with life in prison without parole.
coding_guide: Agree: supports Proposition 133. Disagree: opposes Proposition 133.

text: Hunting and fishing should be a right protected in the state constitution.
coding_guide: Agree: supports Amendment 83 or a constitutional right to hunt and fish. Disagree: opposes Amendment 83.

text: Voters should have to write an ID number, such as the last four digits of their Social Security number, on their mail ballot envelope.
coding_guide: Agree: supports Amendment 84 or requiring an ID number with mail ballots. General support for voter ID without mention of mail ballots is inferred and coded no stronger than 4. Disagree: opposes Amendment 84 or prefers signature verification alone.

text: Ballot questions should be required to be written at an eighth-grade reading level.
coding_guide: Agree: supports Amendment 85. Disagree: opposes Amendment 85.

text: Only Colorado's independent commission should redraw the state's congressional map, even if other states redraw theirs mid-decade.
coding_guide: Agree: supports Amendment 86, or opposes Colorado redrawing its congressional map mid-decade. Disagree: opposes Amendment 86, or supports Colorado redrawing its map mid-decade, for example in response to other states.

text: Colorado's all-mail ballot election system should stay largely as it is.
coding_guide: Agree: defends Colorado's current election system or calls it secure and accurate. Disagree: calls for major changes, such as ending universal mail ballots, hand counts, removing voting machines or requiring in-person voting. Supporting Amendment 84 alone is not a call for major change.

text: Colorado's state government should challenge the current federal administration's policies in court.
coding_guide: Agree: supports the state's lawsuits against the current federal administration or pledges to continue them. Disagree: criticizes those lawsuits as political or wasteful, or pledges to cooperate with the administration instead.
